decisionsTitle: Every race's «când» is a list where its own box is too narrow for one line — one named time too (amends §600)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01 07:40, a phone screenshot of the race's card on production** — the race there has one named time, no race start: «Iconițele astea tot nu sunt aliniate». The row read «Sâm., 21 nov. ·» on one line and «[clock] 10:00 (start eveniment)» wrapped under it: the clock inside the text column, 28 pixels right of the calendar, the time's digits further right than the date, a «·» dangling at the end of the first line. §600 had made the tidy list only for a race with both named times, and only below a viewport of 412 pixels — so a race with one named time never got it, and a two-times race between 412 pixels and its one-line width still showed the old two-line wrap.

**Decision.** One rule: the «când» row of a race — one named time or two (`whenTimes(...).times` with a `key`) — is the list form (a line per piece, no «·», the clock and the flag hung back into the glyph column under the calendar, so the date and every time start at one left edge) whenever the row's OWN box is narrower than the row's one-line width, and the inline form where it fits. A CSS container query decides, not a viewport media query: the card's text column beside the glyph (`flex: 1 1 auto`, so the size-contained box still fills the line), the hero's answer and the page's answer each declare `container-type: inline-size; container-name: when`, and the pieces take `@container when (max-width: 23em)` for one named time and `32em` for two on the card's short date (the long date's 27em and 36em, below). The em is the container's OWN (css-contain-3 resolves a container condition's em against the query container's font-size): 14 pixels on the card (`cardLine`'s `body2`), 16 on the hero and the page (`body1`). On the 14-pixel card the row is one line at «Sâm., 21 nov. · » 112 + the clock 24 + «10:00 (start eveniment)» 166 plus the gaps, about 22em, and with two times at 112 + 178 + 140 plus the gaps, about 31.5em (§597) — so the thresholds sit just above: 322 and 448 pixels on the card, 368 and 512 on the hero and the page. (A first cut at 20em and 28em, sized as if the card were 16 pixels, switched only below 280 pixels and left the 390-pixel phone, column 298, with exactly the wrap of the photograph; the review caught it.) A reader's larger font moves the threshold with the words; English is shorter, so the same em hold. `CARD_LIST_BELOW_412` and `LIST_BELOW_SM` are gone. The same markup as §600 (`data-when-line`, `data-when-separator`, the hung first glyph); only the at-rule changed. On the page the glyph hangs only below `sm`, where the answer is indented by the glyph column — from `sm` up the label column stands there, so a list there keeps the glyph in its seat; the hero has no glyph column and never hangs.

**The thresholds follow the date's form (a review, 2026-10-01).** 23em and 32em were measured on the card's SHORT date («Sâm., 21 nov.», `dateShort`, below `sm` only), but the same list is drawn where the date is LONG — the card from `sm` up, the page's «Când» and the hero — and «Sâmbătă, 21 nov. 2026 · » is about 75 pixels wider at sixteen: there the one-line row is ≈ 26em with one time and ≈ 35.5em with two, so between the short threshold and that width the old wrap came back (the event page on a 430-pixel phone: an answer of 430 − 32 − 28 = 370 pixels, over 368, needs ≈ 384). So `whenListQuery(namedTimes, date)` keys the threshold by the date's form too. The short date keeps 23em for one named time and 32em for two. The long date takes 27em for one (187 + 24 + 166 ≈ 377 pixels, 23.6em, plus the same margin) and 36em for two (187 + 178 + 140 ≈ 505 pixels, 31.6em, plus the margin). On the card the form follows the breakpoint that picks the date: the container rule is nested under the theme's `down("sm")` with the short thresholds and under `up("sm")` with the long ones (a card whose date keeps its year on a phone, no `dateShort`, takes the long set at every width); the page and the hero always show the long date, so they take the long set alone. `event-facts-pills.test.ts` pins both: the card's markup carries each set inside its media block, the page and the hero only the long one; the e2e's `listForm` now also measures the hang itself — each time's leading glyph (the clock, the flag) within 2 pixels of the calendar glyph's left, and each time's words starting at the date's left — not only the hidden dots, which `flex-basis: 100%` would satisfy with the clock still inside the column.

**The tooltip says it once.** The owner, 2026-10-01 07:55, of two production tooltips on the pills — «circa 350 m diferență de nivel (estimativ)» and «circa 10 km (aproximativ)»: «textul e cam lung, nu are sens să punem și (estimativ) sau (aproximativ) dacă am pus «circa» în față, pentru că e pleonasm». `Event.distanceKmApproximateLong` is now «circa {km} km» / «about {km} km» and `Event.elevationMEstimated` «circa {m} m diferență de nivel» / «about {m} m of elevation gain», in both catalogues; nothing else changes — the short forms keep their «≈», and the long ones are still what stands alone wherever the distance or the climb does (the pill's tooltip and what a screen reader hears, the page's facts, the emails and the calendar entry, §598 and §585), so «circa» alone now says the estimate. No code change: `distanceWords` and `elevationWords` read the same keys.

**What it means at a phone's widths.** The card's text column is at most about 320 pixels at 320, 360, 390 and 412: a two-times race is the three-line list at every phone width (412 included — it was two lines there), a one-named-time race the two-line list at 320, 360 and 390 (at 412 its column of about 320 pixels sits at the 322-pixel threshold). The e2e asserts the list form itself — every «·» `display: none`, every time's piece starting at the date's left edge — not merely the line count, which the old wrap matched too. A desktop card narrower than the threshold gets the list too, which is right.

**Unchanged.** Group runs, series and any bare time (`key: null`): no name, a short row, no list and no container. The emails and the `.ics` are plain text. No new catalogue key (two texts lose their parenthetical, above), no migration, no dependency. A browser without container queries (none since 2023) shows the inline form, as before.
changelogLine: - **The race's «când» lines up with one time too** — the race's card, hero and page draw the date and each named time on a line of their own, the clock and the flag under the calendar, wherever the row's own box is too narrow for one line (a container query, in em, sized for the short and the long date), not only for two times below 412 pixels; and the pills' tooltips say «circa 10 km» without «(aproximativ)», «circa 350 m diferență de nivel» without «(estimativ)». §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Wherever a race's «când» row is narrower than its one-line width — measured on the row's own box, in the row's own font-size: below 23em with one named time and 32em with two where the date is the card's short phone date («Sâm., 21 nov.», below `sm`), below 27em and 36em where it is the long one (the card from `sm` up, the event page, the hero) — the card, the hero and the event page draw it as a list: the date and each named time on a line of their own, no middle dot, and on the card (and on the page below `sm`) the clock and the flag hung in the glyph column under the calendar (their left within 2 pixels of the calendar glyph's) so the date and every time's words start at one left edge; where the row fits it flows inline, and a bare time (a group run, a series) has no list (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

An approximate distance and an estimated climb say «circa» once in their long form and no parenthetical after it — «circa 10 km» / «about 10 km», «circa 350 m diferență de nivel» / «about 350 m of elevation gain» — wherever they stand alone (the pill's tooltip and screen-reader label, the page's facts, the emails, the calendar entry); the pill keeps «≈ 10 km» and «≈ 350 m D+» (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: every race's «când» is a list where its own box is too narrow, one named time too, sized for the short and the long date; the tooltips say «circa» once
